title: Inside the race to build Patriot missiles as stocks run low
summary: Patriot air-defence interceptors have been drained by the wars in Ukraine and with Iran, and demand now far outstrips supply. Correspondent Mike Cerre reports from Kyiv and from Lockheed Martin, where each missile takes over a year to build and the company is expanding capacity, forming joint ventures and developing a cheaper version. Seth Jones of CSIS argues the US failed to build adequate stockpiles, so Ukraine is unlikely to get many more.
focus: Shadow the Lockheed Martin explanation of production capacity and the supply chain, and Seth Jones's answer on stockpiles: concrete supply-and-demand language you can reuse in operations or manufacturing cases.
